correctness.rationale: Let W_P(t)=P+2cos t and theta=arccos(1/4). Its three-frequency recurrence gives F(Phi_P(t))=Phi_P(t+theta). The projective triple map is invertible, except antipodal quotient at P=0; theta/pi irrational because 2cos theta=1/2 is a nonintegral rational algebraic integer contradiction, yielding unique Haar pushforward on each punctured rotation carrier. For P<2, D_P has two simple zeros with derivative absolute 2sqrt(1-P²/4) and nonzero numerator V±, giving precise r^-1 tails. For P=2 the double zero has D≈(t−pi)² and numerator norm sqrt261/4, giving r^-1/2 constant sqrt(a)/pi. For P>2 the positive denominator lower bound gives compact support. Layer cake proves exact moment cutoffs; approximating divergent R^q below by capped observables continuous at poles proves divergence along every complete orbit. Setting t=pi+sqrtδ z gives denominator δ(z²±1), yielding the two limiting arcs lengths. Independently checked 12 conjugacy evaluations and twelve deterministic root-isolation threshold profiles at δ=1e−3 and 2e−4, including zero-plus-side cases. Finite diagnostics do not prove all-orbit limit/unique ergodicity, which follow from the irrational rotation argument.

value.rationale: The studied rational map has a natural projective-conic invariant family with an actual singular geometric transition at P=2. Tail exponents, sharp moment cutoffs and both crossover profiles are physically and mathematically interpretable orbit-sampling invariants not specified by the known existence of conics. The result is narrow but resolves a motivated distributional transition exactly and provides all-orbit divergence beyond almost-sure ergodic statements.

final_claim: For the explicitly conjugated irrational-rotation carriers of F(x,y)=((3x/2−5/4)/y,(x−3/2)/y), the unique invariant probability on each carrier has radial tails order r^-1 (0<=P<2), r^-1/2 (P=2), bounded support (P>2), corresponding moment thresholds and explicit distinct two-sided boundary scaling limits.
